items.title: uk-insolvency: a Gazette data.json body that arrives empty or shorter than its content-length is retried like a 5xx and, after the retries, keeps the previous snapshot without an error row
items.why: Daily numbers 2026-09-30: `uk-insolvency (thegazette.co.uk page results-page=1: Unexpected end of JSON input after 3 reads (0 bytes, content-length declared))`; 09-28 the same `Unexpected end of JSON input`; 09-27 and 09-29 a 500 (retry shipped 09-29, `gazette-5xx-retry`). Four days without a fresh insolvency snapshot on a live surface. The source (`src/sources/uk-insolvency.ts`) already reads the body up to three times; a zero-byte body with a declared content-length is the origin closing the stream early, so: treat a short body exactly like a 5xx (fair-use pause, one more read), and when every read fails, log `refresh_log` status `skipped` with the message and keep the previous KV snapshot (Blind Mode already serves it) rather than `error`, so the row shows a stale-since date instead of a daily error. Verify the current response shape through the relay first (`GET RANGE=0-4095` of the data.json URL with the corporate notice types). Id follows the `refresh-<slug>` convention of scripts/refresh-errors-to-queue.ts so the 06:30 job extends this item instead of filing a second one. Built 2026-09-30 (burn-down): relay check showed the Gazette serving the full 204 KB page-1 body (100 notices) to a runner while the Worker read 0 bytes, so the cut is momentary and size-related: page size 50, a cut body (empty or shorter than content-length) retried four times with growing fair-use pauses (~13 s), and a later page that never arrives keeps the pages already read (warn `partial_snapshot`) instead of failing the day. The `skipped` refresh_log status is NOT added: the table's CHECK allows only ok/error (a migration for a rebuild) and the error row is exactly what `refresh-errors-to-queue` keys on — hiding it would hide the outage. KV keeps a stale snapshot 7 days, so the 2026-09-26 snapshot expires ~10-03 without a good refresh.
items.proof: uk-insolvency absent from `refresh errors` for 7 consecutive days; the snapshot's newest notice date within 2 days of today

items.title: uk-insolvency: refresh has failed 2 times in the last 4 days — fix the source or keep the last snapshot without an error row

items.title: Change-feed mode on every Apify actor (`mode: changes`, `since`, `change`) so a scheduled run is a register monitor
items.why: Research 2026-10-05 (starved pipeline): Apify is the only shelf with runs from outside the repo (Daily numbers 10-01..10-04: +12/+11/+16 runs a day, 17 users/30d — the `ours/others` split starts in the 10-05 row, so part of that may be Apify QA), while the change feeds — the one thing no rival sells (STRATEGY §5, 2026-09-24) — read `changes 7d: 0 (mcp 0, rest 0)` on every row since the counter exists (09-30). The 17 actors call only /v1/data (shared `src/gankdat.mjs`; no actor folder has a changes input), so an Apify user cannot schedule "what is new this week" — and scheduled runs are the Store's recurring-revenue mechanic (Schedules + pay per result). items.title: Authed MCP probe without an owner secret: the metrics runner mints a one-run probe key in D1, probes with it, deletes it
items.why: Research 2026-10-09: the 10-08 row's `mcp probe` reads `authed: n/a (no GANKDAT_PROBE_KEY)` — the keyed path (the one Glama's test profile and every paying client use) is never probed, and a GANKDAT_PROBE_KEY repository secret is an owner action. api_keys stores only the SHA-256 of a key (migration 0002), and the runner already writes D1 through the REST API, so it can generate a random key per run, insert its hash for an internal probe account (`probe@gankdat.com`, excluded from the accounts reading like the other internal addresses), run the three authed calls, then delete the row — no secret, no owner. Do: scripts/mcp-probe.ts takes the key from runner-refresh's hand-off (or mints it itself with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN), the row reads `authed: init 200, tools 200, call 200`; a leftover row from a killed run is deleted on the next run; tests for mint/delete and the exclusion. Built 2026-10-09 (burn-down): mcp-probe.ts mints the key itself (`withProbeKey`: GANKDAT_PROBE_KEY wins, else mint with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, probe, delete the D1 row and the Worker's `key:<hash>` KV copy in a finally; the next mint sweeps a killed run's row), a failed mint reads `authed: n/a (mint failed: …)` and lists under refresh errors; the probe step gets CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN in docs/ci/gankdat-metrics.yml (installer moves it); metrics.mjs skips the probe's user agent in the MCP 24h, change-feed and datasets-30d traffic counts. 8 tests. Push runs mint too (three cheap REST calls), so the fill row carries the reading as well.
items.proof: the Daily numbers row carries an authed probe reading every day with no new repository secret

items.title: uk-trademark-journal: refresh has failed 2 times in the last 4 days — fix the source or keep the last snapshot without an error row
items.why: Filed by the 06:30 metrics job (scripts/refresh-errors-to-queue.ts): the Daily numbers rows list uk-trademark-journal under refresh errors on 2026-10-08 (no successful refresh since 2026-10-04); search: n/a (no SEARCH_CONSOLE_KEY secret; owner action 020) and 2026-10-09: no successful refresh since 2026-10-04 after the fix of refresh-uk-trademark-journal (2026-10-07). The surface serves the last good snapshot meanwhile (Blind Mode). Read ventures/gankdat/src/sources/uk-trademark-journal.ts, verify the origin's current response through the relay before changing the parser, and make a transient origin fault log `skipped` rather than `error` once retries are exhausted. Built 2026-10-09 (build): the first wave-log reading showed no line from the 06:05 wave at all, only request lines; reproduced offline — the hash backfill's page UPDATE (`UPDATE … FROM` a json_each subquery) made SQLite walk all 162k rows and scan the 2,000 entries for each, 200 s a page in SQLite and longer on D1, so the wave was killed before the budget check between pages could write the skipped row. Fix in d1store: the entries are a MATERIALIZED CTE, so SQLite loops over them and probes rows by primary key (0.03 s a page; plan asserted on D1 in the spec); a backfill that throws writes an error row; a backfill over 3 min hands the delta to the next night (BACKFILL_HANDOVER_MS). The origin was never the problem: no request reached the IPO on 10-08/10-09. Expect a skipped-then-ok pair of rows by 10-11.
items.proof: uk-trademark-journal absent from refresh errors for 7 consecutive Daily numbers rows

items.title: RFC 7591 dynamic client registration for the OAuth server: `/register` (public clients, PKCE, redirect_uris stored), `registration_endpoint` in the RFC 8414 metadata, `/authorize` accepting a registered client_id beside a CIMD URL
items.why: Found building the Docker MCP Catalog entry (2026-10-10): Docker's gateway starts OAuth for a remote server only through RFC 7591 — `PerformDCR` fails with "no registration endpoint found" when the RFC 8414 document has none (docker/mcp-gateway, vendor/github.com/docker/mcp-gateway-oauth-helpers/dcr.go:121) — and Cursor, ChatGPT and VS Code register clients the same way; only Claude uses client-id metadata documents, so the 2026-09-30 OAuth hop works for Claude alone and the Docker entry ships without an `oauth` block. Build: a D1 table (or KV, 30-day TTL) of registered public clients keyed by a random client_id with client_name, redirect_uris (https or loopback, same rules as CIMD), `token_endpoint_auth_method: none`; `/register` rate-limited per IP like /authorize; `/authorize` and `/token` resolve a registered id first, then CIMD; consent page names the registered client_name; `oauth_funnel` points carry the client kind. Then a second docker/mcp-registry PR adds `oauth: [{provider: gankdat, secret: gankdat.personal_access_token, env: GANKDAT_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}]` and the Toolkit handles sign-in in the browser. Effort 0.5 day, 0 owner minutes. 2026-10-10 burn-down: built as POST /register (D1 oauth_clients, migration 0016, v0.23.0): public clients, 1-10 redirect URIs (https dotted host or http loopback), auth method none, PKCE; client_id gkcl_<label>_<hex> carries the display host so consent, the oauth:<label> key and the funnel work unchanged; registration_endpoint in the RFC 8414 document; funnel steps registered/register_rejected; 6 tests. The Docker oauth block waits for the first catalog PR (ALERTS handoff) to be listed.
items.proof: a `token` step in the Daily numbers row's `oauth funnel 7d` for a client host other than claude.ai within 30 days of deploy; the Docker entry's oauth block merged
